pages.text: H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O as a current. The open-circuit voltage is the Nernst voltage, E = E° + (RT/2F)·ln(p_fuel·√p_O₂). Drawing current costs voltage three ways: activation (Tafel, 0.06·ln(i/i₀)), resistance (0.2 Ω·cm²) and, near the limiting current, mass transport. Power is V·i: it peaks part-way.
$(thing)Set$(): Load current density, Fuel pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Membrane humidity: the resistance varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The cell is flooded: too little current to carry its water off; The cell is starved of fuel.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power follows the power density.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Nernst voltage: E = E° + (RT/2F)·ln(p·√p_O₂)$(br)Cell voltage: V = E − 0.06·ln(i/i₀) − R·i + 0.05·ln(1 − i/i_L)$(br)Power density: P = V·i
